requirementsText:
User Management API:
- POST /users — Create a new user with email, name, and password. Returns 201 with user object.
- GET /users/:id — Get user by ID. Returns 200 with user or 404 if not found.
- PUT /users/:id — Update user profile. Returns 200 with updated user.
- DELETE /users/:id — Delete user. Returns 204. Requires admin role.
- GET /users — List all users. Supports pagination with page and limit query params.

expectedSuccess.description: Returns created user object with id, email, name, createdAt

businessRules: Password must be at least 8 characters

requirements.description: Retrieve a user by their ID
businessRules: Returns 404 if user does not exist

testCases.name: Create user with valid data
testCases.description: POST with all required fields should create user and return 201
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns user object with generated ID, email, name, and createdAt timestamp

verdict.analysis: Test was skipped in dry-run mode. Based on the payload structure and API design, this test case is well-formed and should pass against a real endpoint.

testCases.name: Create user with missing email
testCases.description: POST without email field should return 400/422
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns error response indicating email is required

verdict.analysis: Dry run skipped. Negative test correctly omits required email field.

testCases.name: Create user with duplicate email
testCases.description: POST with existing email should return 409 conflict
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns conflict error indicating email is already taken

verdict.analysis: Cannot verify conflict detection in dry-run mode. The test design is correct but requires execution against a seeded database.
issues: Cannot verify conflict detection without real API execution
suggestions: Seed test database with an existing user before running this test
Run in non-dry-run mode to validate conflict handling

testCases.name: Get user by valid ID
testCases.description: GET with a valid user ID should return 200 with user object
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns user object with id, email, name, createdAt

verdict.analysis: Test is well-structured with a realistic path parameter. Should succeed against a populated database.

testCases.name: Get user with non-existent ID
testCases.description: GET with an ID that does not exist should return 404
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns 404 with error message indicating user not found

verdict.analysis: Correctly tests 404 behavior with a clearly non-existent ID.

testCases.name: Update user without authorization
testCases.description: PUT without a valid auth token should return 401/403

verdict.analysis: Auth test correctly uses an invalid token. Should return 401 from a properly implemented endpoint.

testCases.name: Delete user without admin role
testCases.description: DELETE without admin role should return 403 forbidden
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns forbidden error indicating admin role required

verdict.analysis: Cannot fully validate role-based access control without a real token representing a non-admin user.
issues: Role distinction cannot be tested in dry-run mode
suggestions: Use a real non-admin JWT token when running against live API
Set up test users with different roles in your test environment

testCases.name: Create user with invalid email format
testCases.description: POST with malformed email should return 400
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns validation error for invalid email format

verdict.analysis: Good edge case testing email format validation.

testCases.name: Create user with empty password
testCases.description: POST with empty string password should return 400
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns validation error indicating password is too short

verdict.analysis: Tests empty password validation. Most APIs return 400 for empty required string fields.

testCases.name: List users with pagination
testCases.description: GET /users with page and limit params should return paginated results
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns array of users with pagination metadata (total, page, limit)

verdict.analysis: Pagination parameters are correct but cannot verify response shape (pagination envelope vs flat array) without execution.
issues: Cannot verify response includes pagination metadata in dry-run
suggestions: Confirm API returns pagination envelope: { data: [], total, page, limit }
Consider testing with limit=1 to verify single-item pagination

testCases.name: Delete existing user with admin token
testCases.description: DELETE with valid admin token should return 204

verdict.analysis: Cannot verify delete operation in dry-run mode. A real admin token is needed.
issues: Placeholder admin token will not work against real API
suggestions: Provide a real admin token via the authToken field when starting the run
Ensure the test user ID exists before the delete test runs

testCases.name: Get user with invalid ID format
testCases.description: GET with non-numeric or malformed ID should return 400 or 404
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns error for invalid ID format

verdict.analysis: Path traversal attempt in ID field — good security-focused edge case. A well-implemented API should sanitize this.
suggestions: Verify the API sanitizes path parameters to prevent path traversal attacks

summary:
This dry-run test of the User Management API generated 12 comprehensive test cases covering happy paths, negative scenarios, edge cases, and authentication checks. Of the 12 tests analyzed, 8 passed the structural review, 3 were flagged as failures due to dry-run limitations (particularly around conflict detection and role-based access), and 1 received a warning regarding pagination response shape.

The primary recommendation for the development team is to run this test suite in live execution mode against a properly seeded test environment. Specifically: (1) Seed the database with at least one existing user to test conflict detection, (2) Create test users with different role levels (admin vs regular) and provide real JWT tokens, and (3) Confirm the pagination response envelope matches the expected format. The test suite structure is solid and will provide meaningful coverage once executed against the real API.
